– Infinite regress
Infinite regress: A word is explained by another word, which is explained by a third, ad infinitum
“Empathy is imagined sympathy is feeling compassionate is feeling kindhearted is…”
“A rose is a flower is a plant is an organism is a molecule structure is a…”
“A molecule is a group of bonded atoms is a group of protons, electrons, and neutrons is a group 
of quarks and gluons is a…” ad infinitum
Infinite regress is a fallacy of all science but unavoidable; a limitation of human understanding
If you loop back infinite regress to its own beginning, it becomes full circle:

Gottlob Frege 
(1892)
The ‘sense’ of the word is its presentation form
The reference of a word is to something existing in the real world 
(according to the observer’s beliefs)
The famous example is that ‘the second planet from the sun’ may be 
called ‘Venus’ as well as ‘the morning star’ and ‘the evening star’ 
(although it is not a star at all)
All three expressions are synonyms for that one particular planet
The ‘sense’ of a word emphasises a particular aspect of the entity it refers to, conjuring up an 
image, a ‘mock thought’ or ‘Scheingedanke’ about that entity

– Triangulation
Triangulation does not really solve the issue of infinite regress but it is the best we can do. It 
relates different types of observations (measurements) together
Therefore, you need theory, even if you think you do applied work only
The theory should say what the different measures should show to confirm / reject the 
concepts that the theory relies on
For instance: metaphor theory
Example of metaphor use is to present ‘quarks as building blocks’ (Huang, 1992: p. 25)
Triangulation means that the researcher employs various methods and/or data sets to gain a 
more encompassing understanding of observable events and in doing so, designing more 
opportunities for falsification
Huang, K. (1992). Quarks, leptons & gauge fields. London: World Scientific.
15/87

Denzin (1970, p. 301) discerns four types of triangulation
Data triangulation: Different time periods, various spaces, various samples of people (cf. ‘waves’)
Investigator triangulation: Different researchers doing the same study (cf. replication studies)
Theory triangulation: More theories explain the same phenomenon, outcome predictions differ 
(e.g., comparison theory of metaphor vs anomaly theory vs interaction theory)
Methodological triangulation: Different types of data sampled through different kinds of methods 
(e.g., word association, reaction times, brain potentials)
– Triangulation
To make up a little for the fallacy of infinite regress and gauge the reference of words from 
their sense, triangulation formulates more dimensions on which meanings should 
converge

●Scale construction
Scale construction is a triangulation method to circumvent (up to a degree) the issues with 
‘one item – single response’ surveys. However, infinite regress may still persist but the 
meanings of the words are now ‘intersubjectively’ measured (i.e., using more respondents, 
calculating an ‘average’ meaning over multiple items)
An item can be a question
Do you like sunflowers?
It can be a statement you rate
I like sunflowers
Questions tend to beg for nominal and ordinal measures: no | somewhat | yes
Statements tend to invite ordinal to interval measures:
1 – 2 – 3 – 4 – 5 – 6
(I prefer the latter)
Be aware of terminology:
Measurement scale
Multiple items that measure the same concept 1
Rating scale
Numerical assessment of an item on ordinal or interval level
1 Also called a psychometric scale
21/87

– Bipolar vs unipolar measurement scales
Speed scale
My system is:       slow  0—1—2—3—4—5  fast
This Speed scale uses a ‘semantic differential,’ putting two opposites on one dimension
This way of measuring assumes that fast and slow are mutually exclusive (fast = 1 — slow)
It is a bipolar conception of speed:
- Less fast is equal to more slow
- More fast is equal to less slow
Most of the time, human experience is NOT bipolar; it is a little bit of everything in relation 
to one another (e.g., “I love and hate methods class”)
In other words, time experience may be unipolar. One unit of less fast may be experienced 
as two units of more slow. This is a unipolar conception of speed. The subscales should be 
treated as relatively independent

You have to query the dimensions that are responsible for Appreciation, Satisfaction, etc.
Hence, theoretical analysis before measurement

‘Single item – one response’ gauges Frege’s sense of a 
word but ignores the different meanings people may 
attribute (Frege’s reference). Every word is explained by 
another word, leading to the fallacy of infinite regress
We can only measure sense but to infer the reference as 
well, we try for triangulation, defining more dimensions 
on which meanings should converge
As a form of triangulation, we learned to do scale 
construction:
– Do concept analysis first
– Formulate multiple items
– Use unipolar measurement scales (not bipolar)
– Consisting of indicative and contra-indicative items
– In the form of statements

ummary
With rating scales, researchers often include a ‘neutral’ 
position, which is not smart, because respondents use 
that as an escape like ‘not applicable’
Use 6-point rating scales, starting from 0 to 5, “totally 
disagree” to “totally agree,” respectively. Averaging over 
indicative and contra-indicative items will show whether 
participants are neutral, hitting scale midpoint (= 2.5)
Do not use semantic differentials because opposites are 
not always diametrical and so the psychological distance 
between poles differs. People then have to invest effort 
in reading the scale labels all the time
During scale construction, avoid:
– Double negations
– Ambiguity
– Extremes
– Quantities
– Long sentences, difficult words
– Appreciation scales (like-dislike)
